discrepancies.kind: missing-list is wrong; recoverable T1/T2 evidence declared unsourced
discrepancies.summary: Six of the twelve 'missing' entries are refuted. The Wayback archive holds fully populated responses from CME's own trading-hours service (T2) for every one of the six 2024 U.S. holidays the deliverable declares unsourced, at the very capture instants the deliverable already used for other windows.
discrepancies.detail: The deliverable's stated reason is 'the service returns hasEvents:false with empty event arrays for dates already past, so only Wayback captures taken before a holiday carry data'. That is false for 2024 dates. I re-fetched each window from capture 20240708161439 (the same crawl instant that produced the accepted api_2024-09-01.json and api_2024-11-27.json) and from 20241220155339/40: fromEventDate=2024-01-14 -> hasEvents:true, 66 events; 2024-02-18 -> true, 66; 2024-03-28 -> true, 22; 2024-05-26 -> true, 66; 2024-06-18 -> true, 88; 2024-07-03 -> true, 69. The real behaviour is a retention window that, as of the 2024-07-08 crawl, covered calendar 2024 and not 2022/2023; the 2022-12-31 negative control was generalised into a rule it does not support. The evidence was already in hand: raw/cme-2022-2024/cdx_svc.json contains all twelve CDX rows, and the working note raw/cme-2022-2024/api_targets.txt already lists five of the six exact URLs. For MLK the working note picked the 20260831004234 capture, which is the one capture that does return hasEvents:false, and the conclusion was extended to the other five without probing them.
recoverable_instants_examples: Good Friday 2024-03-29: all ten representative products (ZN, ES, CL, ZC, 6E, GC, LE, BTC, CSC, LBR) have empty event arrays for eventDate 2024-03-29 and no evening reopen on 2024-03-28 -> full calendar-day closure; CSC prints 13:55 closed on 2024-03-28.

Memorial Day 2024-05-27: ES and ZN 12:00 preopen then 17:00 open (tradingDate 2024-05-28); CL and GC 13:30 preopen then 17:00 open; 6E and BTC 16:00 preopen then 17:00 open; ZC 19:00 open; LE and LBR no events.

Independence Day 2024: ES 12:15 closed on 2024-07-03 (an early close the deliverable records nowhere), ZN/CL/GC/6E/BTC 16:00 closed on 2024-07-03, ZC full day session then 16:00 closed with no evening reopen; on 2024-07-04 ZN/ES 12:00 preopen + 17:00 open, CL/GC 13:30 preopen + 17:00 open, 6E/BTC 16:00 preopen + 17:00 open, ZC/LE/LBR no events.
MLK 2024-01-15 and Presidents Day 2024-02-19: ES/ZN 12:00 preopen + 17:00 open; CL/GC 13:30 preopen + 17:00 open; 6E/BTC 16:00 preopen + 17:00 open; ZC 19:00 open; LE/LBR no events.

discrepancies.summary: Four family entries quote a 'TRADE DATE' label from a table cell that is in fact empty.
discrepancies.detail: Coordinate extraction (pdftotext -bbox-layout) of christmas-day-2023.pdf shows the MONDAY, 25 DECEMBER 2023 column at x=196.8 carries 'TRADE DATE: TUES 26 DEC' only at the INTEREST RATE, EQUITIES, ENERGY, FX, METALS, CRYPTOCURRENCIES and DAIRY rows (y=398/477/557/778/858/1022/1101); there is no entry at the GRAINS row (y=681), the LIVESTOCK row (y=954) or the LUMBER row (y=1180). The same holds for new-years-day-2024.pdf: the MONDAY, 1 JANUARY 2024 column at x=226.4 has entries at y=390/469/549/770/850/1014/1093 and nothing at GRAINS (y=673), LIVESTOCK (y=946) or LUMBER (y=1172). The affected entries are 2023-12-25 globex_grains, 2023-12-25 globex_livestock, 2024-01-01 globex_grains and 2024-01-01 globex_livestock, each of which states that the Monday cell 'prints only TRADE DATE: TUES 26 DEC / TUES 2 JAN'. It prints nothing. The derived status ('closed') is unaffected, and the parallel lumber entries correctly say 'no time events'.

discrepancies.summary: 'early_close' is applied systematically to families whose printed holiday halt instant is identical to their ordinary daily close instant, which would produce no-op or misleading holiday-table rows.
discrepancies.detail: On the Monday-holiday documents CME prints '16:00 (PREOPEN) HALT' for FX and CRYPTOCURRENCIES while printing 12:00 for EQUITIES/INTEREST RATE and 13:30 for ENERGY/METALS. 16:00 CT is the ordinary final-close instant for those families, so what is non-normal on those days is the trade-date skip and the longer preopen window, not an earlier close. The deliverable nonetheless records status 'early_close' with a 16:00 instant for globex_fx and globex_cryptocurrency on 2022-05-30, 2023-05-29, 2023-06-19, 2023-09-04 and 2024-09-02 (and on 2024-09-02 the T2 rows for 6E and BTC are 16:00 preopen / 17:00 open with no closed event at all). The verbatim fields preserve the printed text faithfully, so this is a defect in the derived classification rather than in the evidence, and because the convention is applied consistently it can be corrected by one re-classification rule. The same question arises for the 2023-07-03 INTEREST RATE / FX / ENERGY / METALS rows, which the deliverable does classify as 'normal' at 16:00 - so the convention is not even internally consistent between the Monday-before-a-holiday case and the holiday-Monday case.

discrepancies.summary: Fifteen entries use the family key 'globex_energy (ENERGY line)' and fifteen use 'globex_energy (METALS line)' rather than the served key spelling.
discrepancies.detail: The split faithfully records that the 2023 one-pagers and the T2 service print ENERGY and METALS as separate lines with genuinely different instants (13:30 vs 13:30 on holiday Mondays, but 12:45 for both on the 2023-11-24 half day and 12:45/12:45 on 2024-12-24), which is useful information. But because NYMEX energy and COMEX metals share one served key, a consumer reading this file cannot mechanically key on 'family'. Recommend a separate 'line' field rather than decorating the key.
